args: Determines the quality of the collision detection. Discrete mode is much faster, but less accurate. Continuous mode prevents objects from passing through each other at high velocities. Dynamic mode switches between the two based on velocity.
When enabled, entities will reset their animation override if they are damaged. For example, a human will stop walking when shot.
When enabled, humans and androids will drop objects when their arms aren't capable of holding on anymore. This is usually when they die or when their arms are shot. Default is on.
Adjust the intensity of the screenshake. Default is 1x.
Toggle whether selection, freezing, and wire highlights are drawn or not. Useful for recording.
Determines how much slower the time will pass in slow motion mode. Default is 20%.

Heat will travel through the air when this is enabled.
If disabled, heat can only be transferred through heat pipes and direct contact.
This setting may decrease performance when enabled. It is disabled by default.

Determines the amount of physics iterations for the physics simulation. Higher values cause the simulation to be more accurate at the cost of performance. Values greater than 128 may have diminishing returns. Default is 32.
The distance between grid points used for translational snapping. This helps in aligning objects more precisely by snapping their position to the nearest grid point. Default is 0.25 m
The angle increment used for snapping during rotation. This helps in aligning objects more precisely by snapping their rotation to the nearest multiple of this value. Default is 15 degrees
Alert when mods significantly affect loading times
When enabled, an alert will appear when mods cause increased loading times.

When enabled, the game will reject mods with suspicious code. Takes effect after restart. 
<color=#F55><b>It is recommended to keep this enabled. Mods that ask you to disable this setting should be reported.
The maximum amount of seconds that a mod can compile for until it's skipped.
No blood or obvious gore will be rendered when this is enabled.
Enabling this will cause the generation of procedural flesh and bone fragments on full limb crush. This may cause performance issues when lots of limbs are destroyed.
The higher this value is the more fragile entities become.
Toggle whether limbs are fully destroyable or not. When enabled, limbs will turn into red mist under extreme pressure.
Toggle whether brain damage can occur. It causes organisms to occasionally pass out, fail to stand upright, and have seizures.
Toggle whether limbs explode when too full of liquid. Disabled by default. Will only take effect if limb crushing is enabled.
Wounds and injuries will slowly heal on living organisms when this is enabled.
Limbs with enough flesh on them may eject chunky particles when shot.
Dismemberment of limbs may expose loose stringy tissue.
Determines how much force is needed to crush a limb. Default is 100%.
Bloom is a post processing effect that gives the illusion of objects being extremely bright.
Toggle whether bullets have travel time and display tracers. This degrades performance. Off by default.
This will toggle relatively performance-heavy effects.
Toggle whether decals are created. Disabling decals may improve performance.
The lighting system makes dark areas actually dark, and makes light-emitting objects useful. Disabling lighting will make everything "full bright". Lighting has very little impact on performance.
The volume of the entire application.
The volume of all items and effects in the game.
The volume of the ambient hum and other background noises.
Highpass cutoff. Ambient audio will not play any audio below this frequency. This is useful if you suffer from crackling audio issues. 90 Hz is the default and recommended value here.
Audio can play at volumes that exceed set limits. It is recommended you keep this turned on to prevent hearing damage. You enable this at your own risk!
When enabled, things like explosions and guns can be heard reflecting and echoing in the distance. Disabling this setting makes audio processing a bit less demanding.
When enabled, supersonic bullets can make whip crack and whiz-by sounds.
Debug messages will be logged as notifications in-game. Messages include warnings, errors, and unhandled exceptions. It is recommended to keep this off.
Displays the current framerate in the top-right of the screen.
Determines how fast zooming using the mouse wheel is. Default is 1x.
How often should the thermal vision be updated?
Toggle whether wires block the context menu for the underlying object.
Determines the temperature unit used throughout the game. Celsius by default.
With Vsync turned on, the framerate will be capped to the refresh rate of your monitor. This minimises screen tearing.
Anti-aliasing attempts to get rid of jagged edges.
Change the way HDR colours are displayed.
Modify the final exposure value. Default is 100%

Downscale the resolution that the game is being rendered at.
<b><color=#ff9>This only applies when the window mode is set to Borderless or Fullscreen.

Determine the upper bound of the framerate.
<color=#ff9><b>This will only take effect if Vsync is disabled.
A simplified background may help decrease compression artifacts in screen recordings. Simplified rendering does not increase performance.
Determines the way the window is presented.
